task: PR #1193's named next lever / decode-engine-init-resolve-cache.json named_next_lever: memoize Lark's InteractiveParser.accepts() by parser-automaton state rather than token history, with an I3/I6 safety proof, since automaton state genuinely repeats across different token histories reaching the same LALR state (unlike the _tail witness-search cache's literal-history key, PR #1192's 0-hit finding).

lark_internals_investigated.purity_confirmed: accepts() copies the parser, strips callbacks, and probes with Token instances built from the bare Token class (LexerThread._Token = Token) -- no lexer/position state read; value-stack contents never inspected (only len). accepts() is a pure function of (parse_table, state_stack).
lark_internals_investigated.top_of_stack_only_key_is_unsound: ParserState.feed_token's reduce action pops `size` frames off state_stack and re-checks the SAME lookahead token against the state now exposed BELOW the popped frames -- that state is part of the left context, not determined by the top state alone. Two different histories sharing only the top-of-stack state can expose different states below after a reduce and legally disagree on accepts()'s outcome. Proven concretely by a synthetic 2-branch grammar (test_top_of_stack_alone_is_not_a_sound_key).
lark_internals_investigated.sound_key_identified: tuple(state_stack) (ints, IntParseTable is the default LALR table type) plus the parse_table object itself (not id(), to avoid id-reuse after eviction/GC) -- ParserState.copy() never copies parse_conf, so every InteractiveParser.copy() from one Lark.parse_interactive() call shares the identical parse_table reference.

change_summary: Added a module-level cache in src/slm_training/dsl/grammar/fastpath/engine.py: _cached_ip_accepts(ip), keyed on (ip.parser_state.parse_conf.parse_table, tuple(ip.parser_state.state_stack)) -> frozenset[str], LRU-bounded at 4096 entries. _refresh_accepts() (used by both reset() and every _sync) now calls it instead of self._ip.accepts() directly. accepts_cache_info()/_accepts_cache_clear() are test/measurement hooks.
safety_argument: Pure memoization of a provably pure function (accepts() depends only on state_stack + the immutable per-grammar parse_table). Keying on the table object (not id()) avoids id-reuse hazard since the dict key holds a strong reference. test_cached_accepts_byte_identical_to_uncached_on_real_prefixes proves byte-identical output across 6 growing real prefixes; test_top_of_stack_alone_is_not_a_sound_key documents why the (rejected) simpler top-only key would be unsound; test_build_completion_forest_unchanged_with_accepts_cache / test_completion_domain_unchanged_with_accepts_cache reconfirm PREFIX8/PREFIX9 n_paths/coverage/candidate-count are unchanged.

reproduction.method: Direct in-process calls to _openui_completion_domain on PREFIX8 ('root = Card([b1') and PREFIX9 ('root = Card([b1,') -- same prefixes as PR #1171/#1172/#1191/#1192 -- with the accepts cache live vs monkeypatched to call ip.accepts() directly (uncached baseline). Both paths warmed once first so _load_parser/_load_lexer/regex caches are equally hot before timing.

measured_before_after.cprofile_note: InteractiveParser.accepts() dropped out of the top-20-by-cumulative-time entries post-fix (pre-fix: 4th highest, 9.08s cumulative / 16,215 calls). Remaining cost is genuine lexing (_lex_tokens/lex/next_token, ~4.5s) and the witness search's own recursive fan-out (_tail/_tail_from), not Lark's accept-probe.

sync_call_counts_unchanged.note: matches PR #1192's baseline exactly -- this fix reduces work inside each accepts() call, not the number of _sync/witness-search calls

structural cache-hit proof (repeated state_stack across independent engine instances)
synthetic-grammar proof that top-of-stack-only keying is unsound (motivates the full-state_stack key)
